title: Vegetable soup with little pasta
description: Povrtna juha: carrot, celeriac, potato and peas in a light broth with tiny pasta. The everyday starter before a Croatian lunch.
steps: Peel and dice the carrots, celeriac and potato into small cubes. Chop the onion finely.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and soften the onion for 4 minutes. Add the carrot and celeriac and stir for 3 minutes more.
steps.tip: Letting the vegetables sweat in oil first gives the broth a deeper taste.

steps: Pour in {1500 ml} water, add the potato and the crumbled stock cube and simmer for 15 minutes with the lid half on.

steps.text: Add the peas and the pasta and cook for 8 minutes more, until the pasta is soft. Season with pepper and stir in the chopped parsley.
steps.tip: If you plan to freeze some, take those bowls out before adding the pasta and cook fresh pasta when you reheat them.

title: Browned flour soup with egg
description: Prežgana juha: flour toasted in butter, simmered into a smooth soup with paprika and a swirled egg. Old, cheap and comforting.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pot on medium heat, add the flour and stir for 4 to 5 minutes until it smells nutty and turns light brown.
steps.tip: Keep stirring and do not let it go dark brown, or the soup turns bitter.

steps: Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika, then whisk in {1000 ml} cold water a little at a time so no lumps form.
Add the crumbled stock cube, bring to the boil and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring now and then.

steps.text: Beat the egg in a cup and pour it in a thin stream into the simmering soup while you stir, so it sets into soft threads. Season with pepper.
steps.tip: Serve with small cubes of bread toasted in a dry pan, if you like.

title: Cream of cauliflower soup
description: Krem juha od cvjetače: cauliflower and a little potato blended smooth with a splash of cream and a pinch of nutmeg.
steps: Cut the cauliflower into small florets. Peel and dice the potato and chop the onion.
Melt the butter in a pot and soften the onion for 4 minutes without browning.
Add the cauliflower, potato, crumbled stock cube and {1000 ml} water. Simmer with the lid on for 20 minutes, until the cauliflower is very soft.

steps.text: Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season with nutmeg and pepper. Warm through without boiling.
steps.tip: Keep a few small florets aside before blending and drop them back in for some bite.

title: Courgette, pea and basil soup
description: Courgettes and peas cooked briefly with plenty of garlic, then blended bright green with basil and lemon. Inspired by Yotam Ottolenghi.
steps: Slice the courgettes thickly and peel the garlic cloves.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot on medium heat and cook the whole garlic cloves for 3 minutes until golden at the edges.
steps.tip: Whole cloves turn sweet and mild instead of sharp.

steps: Add the courgettes, the crumbled stock cube and {900 ml} water. Simmer for 8 minutes, then add the peas and the basil and cook for 3 minutes more.

steps.text: Blend until smooth, add the lemon juice and pepper and taste for salt.
steps.tip: Short cooking keeps the soup green. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Pumpkin soup with ginger
description: Krem juha od bundeve: pumpkin, carrot and a little ginger blended silky, with a few drops of Slavonian pumpkin seed oil on top.
steps: Peel the pumpkin, scoop out the seeds and cut it into cubes. Slice the carrot, chop the onion and grate the ginger.
Heat the oil in a pot and soften the onion for 4 minutes. Add the ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add the pumpkin, carrot, crumbled stock cube and {900 ml} water. Simmer with the lid on for 20 minutes, until everything is soft.

steps.text: Blend until smooth and season with pepper. Serve with a few drops of pumpkin seed oil.
steps.tip: If it is too thick, loosen it with a splash of hot water.

title: Stracciatella, Roman egg drop soup
description: Hot broth with eggs, parmesan and a little semolina stirred in so they set into soft rags. Ready in 15 minutes. Inspired by Samin Nosrat's Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat.
steps: Bring {1500 ml} water to the boil with the crumbled stock cubes.
In a bowl beat the eggs with the grated parmesan, semolina, nutmeg, pepper and chopped parsley.

steps.text: Turn the broth down to a gentle simmer. Pour in the egg mixture slowly while you stir with a fork, then leave it for 1 minute until the egg sets into soft rags.
steps.tip: If the broth boils hard the egg turns rubbery, so keep it just bubbling.

steps: Taste for salt and serve at once with a little more parmesan.

title: Potato soup with carrot and celeriac
description: A soft potato soup, half mashed in the pot, with tiny cubes of carrot and celeriac and parmesan. Inspired by Marcella Hazan's Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking.
steps: Peel the potatoes and boil them whole in {1200 ml} water with the crumbled stock cube for 20 minutes, until soft. Keep the water.
Meanwhile chop the onion, carrot and celeriac into very small cubes and cook them gently in the butter and oil for 10 minutes, until soft.

steps.text: Mash the potatoes roughly in their cooking water, so the soup turns creamy but still has some pieces.
steps.tip: Do not blend it: a potato masher keeps the texture light, a blender makes it gluey.

steps: Stir in the soft vegetables and simmer for 5 minutes. Take off the heat, stir in the grated parmesan and the chopped parsley.

title: Clear chicken soup with fine noodles
description: Pileća juha: chicken wings and root vegetables simmered slowly into a golden broth, served with fine noodles. Inspired by Irina Janakievska's The Balkan Kitchen.

ingredients.note: whole peppercorns if you have them

steps.text: Put the chicken wings in a large pot with {2500 ml} cold water and bring slowly to a simmer. Skim off the grey foam that rises.
steps.tip: Starting in cold water and never boiling hard is what keeps the broth clear.

steps: Add the peeled whole carrots, the celeriac in chunks, the halved onion with its skin, the parsley stalks, bay leaves, pepper and salt.
Simmer very gently with the lid half on for 1 hour 20 minutes.
Strain the broth. Slice the carrots back into it and pull the meat off the wings, if you like, for the bowls.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in some of the broth for 4 minutes and serve with chopped parsley leaves.
steps.tip: Broth without noodles freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Tomato and egg drop soup
description: Tomatoes fried until jammy, simmered into a quick broth and finished with ribbons of egg and spring onion. Inspired by Fuchsia Dunlop's Every Grain of Rice.
steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Slice the spring onion. Beat the eggs in a jug.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot on high heat and fry the tomatoes for 4 minutes, pressing them with a spoon, until they collapse.
steps.tip: Frying the tomatoes first gives the soup its colour and sweetness.

steps: Add {1200 ml} water and the crumbled stock cube, bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the spinach, if using.
Pour in the egg in a thin stream, stir once gently and turn off the heat. Season with pepper and scatter over the spring onion.

title: Celeriac and apple soup
description: Krem juha od celera: celeriac, potato and a sour apple blended smooth with a spoon of cream. A cheap and gentle winter starter.
steps: Peel and dice the celeriac, potato and apple. Chop the onion.
Melt the butter in a pot and soften the onion for 4 minutes. Add the celeriac and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the potato, apple, crumbled stock cube and {1000 ml} water. Simmer with the lid on for 20 minutes, until the celeriac is soft.

steps.text: Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season with pepper.
steps.tip: A sour apple balances the earthy celeriac. A few toasted walnuts on top are lovely.

title: Cold cucumber and yogurt soup
description: Tarator: grated cucumber in chilled yogurt with garlic, dill and crushed walnuts. A no-cook summer starter. Inspired by Irina Janakievska's The Balkan Kitchen.
steps: Grate the cucumber coarsely, mix it with the salt and leave it for 5 minutes.
Crush the garlic and chop the dill. Crush the walnuts roughly with the bottom of a glass.

steps.text: Whisk the yogurt with {200 ml} cold water until smooth, then stir in the cucumber with its juice, the garlic, dill and most of the walnuts.
steps.tip: Chill it for at least 30 minutes: the garlic mellows and the soup gets properly cold.

steps: Serve with the rest of the walnuts and a few drops of olive oil on top.

title: Green salad with oil and vinegar
description: Zelena salata: crisp lettuce leaves, a little salt, vinegar and oil. The salad on every Croatian table at lunch.

steps.text: Tear the lettuce into pieces, wash it in cold water and dry it well in a salad spinner or a clean tea towel.
steps.tip: Dry leaves hold the dressing; wet ones make it watery.

steps: Just before eating, sprinkle with salt (and crushed garlic, if you like), then the vinegar and the oil, and toss.

title: Cabbage salad
description: Kupus salata: finely sliced cabbage rubbed with salt, then dressed with vinegar and oil. Cheap all winter and better on the second day.

steps.text: Slice the cabbage as thinly as you can, sprinkle with the salt and squeeze it with your hands for 1 minute, until it softens and gives some juice.
steps.tip: Squeezing with salt makes the cabbage tender without cooking it.

steps: Add the vinegar, oil and pepper, toss and leave for 15 minutes before eating. A few drops of pumpkin seed oil on top make it Slavonian.

title: Beetroot salad
description: Cikla salata: boiled beetroot slices in a sweet and sour dressing. Make it once and it keeps for days in the fridge.

steps.text: Boil the beetroots whole, in their skins, for 40 to 50 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Cool them in cold water.
steps.tip: Bought ready-cooked beetroot works too and saves the hour.

steps: Peel and slice the beetroots thinly.
Mix the vinegar, sugar, salt, oil and {3 tbsp} water, pour over the beetroot and add the horseradish, if using. Leave for 30 minutes before eating.

title: Dalmatian potato salad
description: Krumpir salata: warm sliced potatoes soaked in olive oil and vinegar with onion and parsley. No mayonnaise, the Dalmatian way.
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20 minutes, until just soft.
Slice the onion very thinly. Chop the parsley.

steps.text: Peel the potatoes while still warm, slice them and toss at once with the onion, oil, vinegar, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Warm potatoes soak up the dressing; cold ones only get coated.

steps: Stir in the parsley and leave for 10 minutes before eating.

title: Šopska salad with white cheese
description: Tomato, cucumber, pepper and onion under a snow of grated white cheese. A summer side. Inspired by Irina Janakievska's The Balkan Kitchen.
steps: Cut the tomatoes and cucumber into chunks, the pepper into strips and the onion into thin slices.
Toss with the oil, vinegar, a pinch of salt and the chopped parsley.

steps.text: Grate or crumble the cheese thickly over the top just before serving.
steps.tip: If you have a grilled or roasted pepper, use it instead of the raw one, as they do in Bulgaria.

title: Grated carrot salad with lemon
description: Coarsely grated carrots dressed only with olive oil, lemon and salt. Sweet, crunchy and loved by children. Inspired by Marcella Hazan's Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking.
steps: Peel the carrots and grate them on the largest holes of a grater.

steps.text: Toss with the salt, lemon juice and oil, taste and add a little more lemon if it needs it.
steps.tip: Dress it just before eating so the carrots stay crunchy.

title: Cucumber salad with yogurt and garlic
description: Krastavci s jogurtom: thin cucumber slices in a light garlic yogurt dressing with a pinch of paprika. Lovely with anything grilled.

steps.text: Slice the cucumbers thinly, mix with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then pour off the water.
steps.tip: Salting first stops the salad from turning watery.

steps: Stir the crushed garlic and vinegar into the yogurt, mix with the cucumber and sprinkle with paprika and dill.

title: Cabbage, carrot and apple slaw
description: Crunchy cabbage, carrot and apple in a sharp lemon and olive oil dressing with lots of parsley. Inspired by Samin Nosrat's Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat.

steps.text: Slice the onion very thinly and leave it in the lemon juice for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: The lemon takes the harsh bite out of raw onion.

steps: Slice the cabbage finely, grate the carrot and cut the apple into thin matchsticks.
Toss everything with the onion and its lemon juice, the vinegar, oil, salt and chopped parsley. Taste: it should be bright and a little sharp.

title: Garlic tomato salad
description: Ripe tomato slices with garlic steeped in vinegar, olive oil and basil. Best in high summer. Inspired by Marcella Hazan's Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking.

steps.text: Crush the garlic with the salt and leave it in the vinegar for 20 minutes, then take out the garlic pieces.
steps.tip: The vinegar gets the garlic taste without raw bits in your mouth.

steps: Slice the tomatoes, pour the garlic vinegar and the oil over them and sprinkle with basil.

title: Bean salad with onion and pumpkin seed oil
description: Salata od graha: red beans with thinly sliced onion, vinegar and dark pumpkin seed oil, as they make it in northern Croatia.
steps: Drain and rinse the beans. Slice the onion as thinly as you can.

steps.text: Mix the beans and onion with the vinegar, salt and pepper and leave for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: The vinegar softens the onion and the beans soak up the taste.

steps: Pour over the pumpkin seed oil and scatter with parsley. If you have no pumpkin seed oil, use sunflower oil.

title: Kohlrabi salad with sesame oil
description: Crisp kohlrabi matchsticks salted, then dressed with soy, vinegar, garlic and sesame oil. Inspired by Fuchsia Dunlop's Every Grain of Rice.

steps.text: Peel the kohlrabi and cut it into thin matchsticks. Mix with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
steps.tip: Salting draws out water so the dressing clings and the kohlrabi stays crisp.

steps: Mix with the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, crushed garlic and sesame oil and scatter with sliced spring onion.
